assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: final complete opaque environmental painting for COSYWORLD's Greek ship at sea, DAY.
Input image 1 is the authoritative EDIT TARGET: the existing rainy coastal DAY ship-deck painting.
Input image 2 is a supporting GEOMETRY REFERENCE ONLY: the original NIGHT painting of the same deck. Do not copy its night lighting, lit lamps, coast or stars.

Primary request: this EXACT SAME familiar Greek ship and camera, now on the OPEN SEA in neutral airy DAYLIGHT, with no land and no fixed weather. Make a complete finished painting, NOT a cutout or layer. Keep the full original 1672 x 941 canvas and exact frame.

CHANGE THE ENVIRONMENT ONLY, plus removing the target's visible rain and fog: replace every mountain, wooded bank, island, coastal silhouette and shore light beyond the rail with uninterrupted blue-green open ocean and a clear natural pale-blue daytime sky with a few unobtrusive high fair-weather clouds. The distant sea horizon is a straight level line approximately y=360 in the 1672 x 941 image (355-363 is acceptable), measured from the top. No hill, coastline, bank, island or dark land-like form anywhere, including behind the mast, prow and rigging. No band of fog hiding residual land. Moderate small ripples and restrained open-water swell; clear readable horizon. Remove all visible rain streaks, rain stippling, low mist, fog, storm clouds and weather effects.

STRICT SHIP INVARIANTS: preserve the exact position, silhouette, dimensions, perspective, design and details of the massive left mast with its winding ropes and bronze collar; the cargo/bronze fitting and timber at lower left; the full ivory canvas sail across the top with all seams and edges; EVERY rigging line and pulley block; the left and right carved bulwarks and rails; the tall curled prow at center-right; every deck plank, hatch, crossbeam, bolt, rope knot and coil; both lantern housings and their attachments. Do not shift, crop, rebuild, resize, redesign, remove or invent any part of the ship. The center deck standing area and bottom quarter remain clear and quiet for characters and interface.

DAY LIGHT: natural soft diffuse daylight with the same general off-canvas light from the upper right; warm walnut and ochre wood, aged bronze, ivory sail, blue-green water. The deck should be legible and warm without becoming bleached, glossy or orange. Preserve the wood grain and restrained existing sheen, without droplets, active rain or puddles that assert a storm. BOTH existing lanterns remain UNLIT, with ordinary clear/dull glass; NO flames, amber glow or pools of lamplight. No sun or moon disc, no stars, no sunset.

STYLE: match the exact target painting's tactile, finely detailed painted environmental finish and subtle ink-like edges. Keep the original camera and ship identity unchanged. The sea is spacious and calm enough to read the ship; do not add spectacle.

Avoid: any land, islands, coastal trees, mountains, buildings, shore lights, fog banks, fixed rain, snow, lightning, storms, visible sun/moon, people, creatures, extra ships, modern details, readable text, logos, borders, watermarks, transparent background, cropped rigging or altered mast/prow/lantern positions. This is a forward-facing onboard camera: absolutely NO stern wake in front of the bow or straight white wake running toward the horizon; any tiny movement cue belongs in the water beside the hull.

Output exactly 1672 x 941, full original opaque canvas, no crop, zoom, expansion, reframe or aspect-ratio change.

findings: Full 1672 x 941 canvas preserved; ship geometry and frame visually match rainy coastal edit target and original night reference.
All land removed: uninterrupted sea and sky with straight horizon at approximately y=356.
No visible rain streaks, mist, fog banks, islands, buildings, people, text, extra vessels or forward stern wake.
Both existing lantern fixtures remain unlit.
Warm walnut/ochre ship wood and ivory sail stay readable under airy daylight; existing restrained wet sheen retained.
Central standing space and bottom quarter remain clear.
visual_review.limitation: Generated paint textures are not pixel-identical; the image visually preserves ship geometry rather than guaranteeing exact outside-edit pixel identity.

Primary request: paint only a clear open ocean beneath an indigo night sky. EXACT 1672 x 941 full canvas. A perfectly natural, straight ocean horizon runs horizontally across the entire frame at y=355 pixels measured from the top (about 37.7% of the image height). Above that line is uninterrupted night sky; below it is uninterrupted ocean extending to all three lower canvas edges. Maintain this precise horizon placement so the plate will align behind the existing ship foreground.

Sky: deep indigo and navy matching the reference, restrained small stars and a few subtle wisps of blue cloud. Natural and quiet, no spectacular Milky Way or dense sparkling starfield. NO VISIBLE MOON. The unseen moon is outside the frame at the upper right.

Water: silver-blue, clear dark open ocean with restrained low swell and fine, horizontally foreshortened ripples near the horizon, becoming naturally larger nearer the bottom edge. Quiet silver-blue highlights fall from the off-canvas upper-right moonlight, comparable in color and softness to the reference's visible water. Keep the surface coherent across the full width. No wake, no V-shaped trail, no foam path or beam pointing toward the viewer; the plate is the water AHEAD of a ship, not a trailing wake. No lantern-gold reflections because the lanterns will live on the separate ship layer.

STRICT EXCLUSIONS: zero ship, boat, deck, mast, sail, ropes, rigging, rail, prow, lanterns, furniture, framing objects or silhouettes in the foreground. Zero land, island, peninsula, coastline, riverbank, mountains, hills, trees, harbor structures, shore lights or distant ships. Zero mist, fog, fog banks, hazy ridges, rain, snow, storm, lightning, visible moon, sunrise or sunset. No people, creatures, readable text, logos, labels, borders or watermark.

The image must be fully opaque with continuous painted sky/ocean wherever the original reference had a ship or land. Do not leave cutout holes, alpha transparency, an empty foreground, dark silhouettes, checkerboard or blurred patches. Do not create a full ship scene. attempts.prompt:
Use case: background-extraction.
Asset type: a reusable transparent NIGHT SHIP FOREGROUND layer for COSYWORLD, to be composited over separate sea-and-sky environment paintings.
Input image 1 is the sole authoritative EDIT TARGET: the canonical ship-deck-night.webp at exactly 1672 x 941 pixels.

Primary request: REMOVE ONLY THE BACKGROUND from this image, producing a clean genuine RGBA cutout of the existing ship. This is extraction, not repainting. Preserve the foreground ship's original pixel positions, exact camera, viewpoint, framing, geometry, colors, detailed painterly texture and existing NIGHT lighting as closely as possible.

KEEP every part of the ship: the thick mast at left, every rope wound around it, its bronze collar and foreground bronze fixture, all foreground beams and the entire wooden deck/planking/hatch/bolts, all bulwarks and rails with their carved decorations and metal fittings, the curled prow in its exact center-right position, both lit lantern fixtures, every rope coil on the deck, EVERY THIN RIGGING ROPE and pulley block even where it crosses the sky, and the full existing sail across the upper edge with its seams and frayed edges. Keep all orange lantern glow that falls ON the wooden ship and all cool blue night reflections ON ship surfaces. Do not change or brighten the ship's night lighting.

REMOVE TO EXACT ZERO ALPHA: every pixel of sky, stars, clouds, distant mountains, trees, coast, mist, sea and water reflections outside the ship. Remove these background elements from EVERY opening around the ropes, between rigging lines and mast, beneath the sail, around the curled prow and outside/above the rail. There must be no residual sea or hill silhouettes anywhere in the transparent areas. A transparent opening is truly empty alpha, not filled with grey, checkerboard, black, blue, fog, or a painted backing. Do not retain any glow, atmospheric haze, cast shadow or halo floating outside the physical ship. Use clean antialiased edges at the physical boundaries and preserve fine rope silhouettes.

CANVAS AND REGISTRATION ARE CRITICAL: output the complete original 1672 x 941 canvas, with the ship at the EXACT SAME pixel coordinates and scale. No trimming to the object, no recentering, no moving, no zoom, no rotation, no expansion, no cropping, no padding and no aspect-ratio change. The ship still extends to the original image edges. The entire lower deck remains opaque.

Avoid: repainting or redesigning any ship part, changing lighting or textures, invented hardware, missing/simplified rigging, thickened ropes, broken ropes, disappearing sail, altered prow, retained sky/water/coast, opaque backing, checkerboard painted into the image, white/blue edge halos, vignette, added drop shadow, new objects, people, text, borders or watermark.
Output a single high-quality transparent RGBA PNG with a real alpha channel.
